cmn.definition: a set of fungal threads that colonise the roots of two or more plants at once and so may link them below ground
cmn.excludes: claims about what such a network does, such as moving carbon or signals between trees, which are the matters in dispute

focal-study.field: our usage, following Karst and colleagues
focal-study.definition: one of the 18 field studies on these networks whose later citations the original authors read and coded, 11 on network function and 7 on network structure
focal-study.excludes: the citing papers, which are the units counted inside each focal study

unsupported-citation.field: citation analysis, as coded by Karst and colleagues
unsupported-citation.definition: a citation that credits a focal study with a claim that the original authors judged the study's results do not support
unsupported-citation.excludes: any judgement of ours: every coding in this paper is the original authors'

rate-table.field: our usage for the deposited table
rate-table.definition: the share of one focal study's citations in one calendar year that were coded unsupported, as stored in the deposit without its denominator
rate-table.excludes: a count of citations, which the deposit does not hold

denominator-rebuild.definition: the number of citations a focal study received in a year, recovered by finding the whole number n for which a published count k gives the deposited rate k over n
denominator-rebuild.excludes: a count read directly from any source; years with a rate of zero share what remains of the study's total and are the least certain

negative-binomial.definition: a regression for counts whose variance can exceed their mean, fitted here with a log link so that the fitted rate changes by a fixed factor per year
negative-binomial.excludes: models that weight each year by how many citations it holds

within-study.definition: a regression with its own baseline level for each focal study, so the year slope is estimated only from change inside studies
within-study.excludes: change that comes from which focal studies happen to be cited in early and late years

quasi-poisson.definition: a log-linear count regression whose standard errors are scaled by the observed spread, used here for the within-study model
quasi-poisson.excludes: a full probability model for the counts

citation-weighted.definition: a regression of the number of unsupported citations out of all citations in each study-year on the year, so a year with thirty citations counts thirty times as much as a year with one
citation-weighted.excludes: the equal weight per study-year that a model of the deposited percentages gives

study-resampling.definition: drawing focal studies with replacement, refitting the model each time, and taking the middle 95 percent of the refitted ratios as the interval
study-resampling.excludes: resampling single study-years, which would ignore that citations of one study move together

power.definition: the chance that a test detects an effect of a given size when that effect is real, measured here on planted data with a known doubling
power.excludes: the chance that an effect is real given that the test detected it
